newsitem.title: USA: U.S. layoffs rose 38 pct in May vs April - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. layoffs rose 38 pct in May vs April - report.

text.p: U.S. job-cut announcements totaled 21,004 in May, up 38 percent over the 15,214 job cuts announced in April, according to an employment report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc, an outplacement firm.
The headline figure in May was 31.9 percent less than the 30,845 job cuts announced in May 1996, it said.

"In this extraordinarily competitive economy, companies cannot afford to pass the costs of higher wages on to the consumer," said John Challenger, executive vice president of Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

Challenger said U.S. firms in recent years have turned "the downsizing valve to control wage pressure," resulting in the elimination of unproductive employees and a remaining workforce reluctant to ask for wage increases for fear of losing their jobs.
"Today, many leaner companies need to retain employees while continuing to cut costs. Instead of downsizing, they will increasingly target payroll," he said.
May averaged 1,000 job-cut annoucements per day for 21 business days, the report said.

Taking the lead in layoffs, the insurance industry eliminated 2,600 jobs. It was followed by consumer goods (2,490), commodities (2,150), industrial goods (1,840), computer (1,723), and transportation (1,607), the report showed.
"The era of downsizing is by no means behind us," said Challenger. "The first three months of the year saw relatively high numbers of job-cut announcements, " he added.
The year-to-date number of layoffs totaled 170,475, down 26 percent from the same period last year, the report said.
